items.title: Google continues to accelerate its release cadence with Gemini 4 Neon, delivering a small Intelligen...
items.content:
Google continues to accelerate its release cadence with Gemini 4 Neon, delivering a small Intelligence gain over Gemini 4 Carbon at a ~17% lower Cost per Task

@GoogleDeepMind has released Gemini 4 Neon, its fourth model in just seven weeks. Neon (xhigh) scores 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, 1 point ahead of Gemini 4 Carbon (high) and 3rd overall, behind GPT-6.2 Astra (max) and Claude Fable 5.2 (max). At high effort, Neon matches Carbon (high) at less than half the Cost per Task using Carbon’s standard (non-discounted) pricing.

Key takeaways:

➤ Slight improvement in Intelligence for lower Cost and Time per Task: Neon (xhigh) scores 61 on the Intelligence Index, 1 point ahead of Carbon (high), with small improvements in agentic knowledge work, visual reasoning and coding. It costs $6.44 per task, ~17% less than Carbon ($7.76 at non-discounted pricing), and takes ~21 minutes per task, ~40% less than Carbon (~36 minutes). Neon uses ~15% more output tokens per task, so the lower cost comes purely from its 25% lower token prices ($3/$15 vs $4/$20 per 1M input/output tokens), and the lower time from its higher output speed (~110 vs ~57 output tokens per second)

➤ Competitive with Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.2 on coding agents: With Antigravity CLI, Neon (xhigh) scores 59 on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, 3 points ahead of Carbon (high, 55). It scores in line with Claude Code with Claude Fable 5.2 (xhigh, 58) and Claude Opus 5.5 (max, 58) at a much lower Cost per Task. Gemini 4 Neon in Antigravity has an average Cost per Task of $6.86, compared to $12.61 for Claude Opus 5.5 (max) and $15.47 for Claude Fable 5.2 (xhigh). Neon is available in Antigravity CLI for Pro and Ultra subscribers

➤ Significant improvements in visual reasoning and output presentation quality: In GDP.pdf, Gemini 4 Neon (high) scores 33.4%, 5 points above Carbon (high, 28.4%) and in line with the highest scores measured, while Neon (xhigh) scores 28.0%. On AA-Briefcase, Neon (xhigh) scores 1700 Elo overall and leads on Presentation Quality with 1771 Elo, 45 points ahead of the previous leader Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max, 1726). On Google’s Multimodal Knowledge Agent evaluation (MKA), Neon reaches a Climb WSR of 56%, up 2 points from Carbon and on par with the leader, Claude Fable 5.2 (max, 57%)

Key model details:

➤ Context Window: 1M tokens

➤ Multimodality: Text, image, video, and speech input, with text output

➤ Availability: Gemini 4 Neon is publicly available at launch through Google’s API. Pro and Ultra subscribers can also access it in Antigravity and the Gemini app

➤ Effort levels: Gemini 4 Neon offers four effort levels (low, medium, high, and xhigh) - xhigh was introduced to Gemini models in the recent Hydrogen release

➤ Pricing: $3/$15 per 1M input/output tokens, 50% above Gemini 4 Carbon’s currently discounted price of $2/$10 (which ends on November 30), and 25% below its standard $4/$20. Cached input tokens receive the same 95% discount ($0.15)

We're sharing new data on how AI is changing research at OpenAI.

We find researchers' AI use contin...
items.content:
We're sharing new data on how AI is changing research at OpenAI.

We find researchers' AI use continues to rise exponentially, and agents are completing longer tasks, but human involvement remains central in research. Researchers are also spending more time on safety and alignment, with human effort in these areas growing faster than in any other individual research area.

This report aims to increase transparency around research acceleration and inform the governance of increasingly capable AI. We believe that AI labs should be required to track and publicly report indicators of recursive self-improvement (RSI): the process by which AI accelerates the development of future AI systems. 

Our hope is that this expanded report will help sustain and advance shared measurement norms across the industry.

https://t.co/xyGPcCkPCK

items.title: I'm featured quite visibly on Dan's letter, so it's probably good that I briefly explain why I signe...
items.content:
I'm featured quite visibly on Dan's letter, so it's probably good that I briefly explain why I signed while having friends at Anthropic and a lot of respect for them in general.

I don't fully agree with the wording. I wouldn't have used "reckless", and I didn't know the name of the statement when I signed, which isn't my style. But I agree with the underlying sentiment and decided to sign for two reasons.

First, Anthropic is currently on track to be the most powerful company on earth (and for good reasons, like the quality of the team and product). This level of impact on the world will require a degree of transparency and openness close to, or maybe even higher than, that of a sovereign government, and I'm worried they are not currently on track to reach it. It's a version of "with great power comes great responsibility", applied to social responsibility toward everyone using and impacted by your products.

Second, Dan mentions safety groups who felt unable to sign. I heard the same thing directly from a different crowd: entrepreneurs, executives and researchers who agreed with the concerns but were afraid of consequences for their careers or their access to models. Whether or not that fear is justified, I think it's a first example of the problem above, and a worrying early signal about concentration of power in itself.

I'd genuinely like to be proven wrong on both points, and I think Anthropic has the people to do it.

items.title: Meet Gemini 4 Neon — our newest model that brings frontier-level intelligence with fast end-to-end t...
items.content:
Meet Gemini 4 Neon — our newest model that brings frontier-level intelligence with fast end-to-end task completion across complex software engineering, knowledge work, and science workflows.

Neon brings frontier-level performance to your everyday work and is built to handle complex coding and problem-solving without the wait.

How, you might ask? ⬇️

— Smarter coding: Multi-file debugging and refactoring with targeted, surgical edits
— Grounded answers: Excels at multi-step instruction following and builds on our ongoing progress to curb fabrication, recording our lowest fabrication rate yet in internal Google Antigravity testing
— 1M-token context window: Synthesize massive projects, tables, and charts at once
— Adjustable thinking: Balance and adjust speed and depth on the fly with 4 thinking levels

Watch Gemini 4 Neon run a 12-hour /swarm in @antigravity to reconstruct Alan Turing’s 1936 study from archival photos — complete with a running Universal Turing Machine, the blueprint for modern computing.

items.content_html:
Meet Gemini 4 Neon — our newest model that brings frontier-level intelligence with fast end-to-end task completion across complex software engineering, knowledge work, and science workflows.

Neon brings frontier-level performance to your everyday work and is built to handle complex coding and problem-solving without the wait.

How, you might ask? ⬇️

— Smarter coding: Multi-file debugging and refactoring with targeted, surgical edits

— Grounded answers: Excels at multi-step instruction following and builds on our ongoing progress to curb fabrication, recording our lowest fabrication rate yet in internal Google Antigravity testing

— 1M-token context window: Synthesize massive projects, tables, and charts at once

— Adjustable thinking: Balance and adjust speed and depth on the fly with 4 thinking levels

Watch Gemini 4 Neon run a 12-hour /swarm in @antigravity to reconstruct Alan Turing’s 1936 study from archival photos — complete with a running Universal Turing Machine, the blueprint for modern computing.

items.title: There's basically infinite latent token demand across the economy. The only brake is cost. How much ...
items.content:
There's basically infinite latent token demand across the economy. The only brake is cost. How much you're willing to spend on tokens is determined by your RoI on token spend, of which companies are increasingly mindful.

New models keep increasing the RoI on existing use cases AND the scope of valid use cases. Token consumption can keep going up geometrically for a long time.

Today we’re introducing OCRia-1.5

It’s a new family of document parsing models that push the bounda...
items.content:
Today we’re introducing OCRia-1.5

It’s a new family of document parsing models that push the boundaries of accuracy and cost across multiple document parsing dimensions.

We had just released OCRia-1 a month ago, which set a new SOTA in unified document parsing, but we've only released even more improvements since then.
✅ Tables: Table scores rose from 86.5 -> 90.1 on agentic, 83.2 -> 87.5 on cost-effective
✅ Charts: 74.9->76.8 on agentic, 67.3 -> 73.0 on cost-effective
✅ Forms: +2.6 on agentic, +4.2 on cost-effective
✅ Visual Grounding: +4.1 on agentic, and +11 (!!) points on cost-effective

Together, these models set a new Pareto frontier for document parsing. Our cost-effective OCRia-1.5 is the cheapest and most accurate model for parsing all of tables, charts, forms, handwriting, with high-quality layout.

Blog: https://t.co/9NlhPd6E1s

These scores for all our modes (cost-effective, agentic, agentic plus) reflected within ParseBench-2: https://t.co/PWczfhp0OX

The 38 models it trained have passed 50,000 downloads.

The team’s report says it averaged under 20 minutes of work a day, timing its check-ins to Hugging Face’s daily download update around 10am UTC.

143 GitHub projects use its models, including an Android keyboard with over 1000 stars.

items.title: Last week we released ParseBench-2, our most comprehensive effort to benchmark various document OCR ...
items.content:
Last week we released ParseBench-2, our most comprehensive effort to benchmark various document OCR tools.

It drew quite a bit of ire among our peer document OCR vendors, who offered their own reactions:

---- “This is marketing slop” - vendor 1 who immediately goes and publishes lower-effort marketing slop (*cough benchbench cough*)

---- “everybody is number 1 on their benchmark” - vendor 2 who immediately shows their own benchmark where they’re #1
(also we’re not even #1 on some dimensions! No one actually cared about our efforts to be more fair)

there was some constructive feedback which we’re taking into account and iterating on a new release. But it was mostly masked by some (pretty funny) noise and posturing.

Unlike other vendors, our evals are completely open - no hidden judge prompt, no hidden test dataset, and we actively update the leaderboard from Github/Hugging Face submissions.

If you’re in the market for document OCR, I think ParseBench-2 is probably the most comprehensive resource for comparing different solutions. Even if you completely ignore our parsing solutions or overall score, there’s value in understanding the detailed taxonomy we’ve created over different failure types.

Come check it out! https://t.co/PWczfhp0OX

Also our tech report is extremely detailed and the result of incredible effort from our research team. Come check it out: https://t.co/qNlc5r0mss

"My v...
items.content:
Chargebee CEO @cbkrish predicts banks like JPMorgan won't be able to block AI agents forever.

"My view is eventually everybody has to open up access, because a customer owns a record and their data."

"We don't know whether it is a personal assistant of somebody's agent that is accessing, or is it an authorized agent of other products."

"Today we are all riding on the old mental models, which is, oh, you generate a new API key, I give that access to another one. I think that's still a flawed approach, where we are applying what humans used to do in an agentic context."

"Probably there'll be some level of frustration, but the cautious steps when it comes to finance and banking are going to be necessary."
@chargebee

items.content_html:
Chargebee CEO @cbkrish predicts banks like JPMorgan won't be able to block AI agents forever.

"My view is eventually everybody has to open up access, because a customer owns a record and their data."

"We don't know whether it is a personal assistant of somebody's agent that is accessing, or is it an authorized agent of other products."

"Today we are all riding on the old mental models, which is, oh, you generate a new API key, I give that access to another one. I think that's still a flawed approach, where we are applying what humans used to do in an agentic context."

"Probably there'll be some level of frustration, but the cautious steps when it comes to finance and banking are going to be necessary."

@chargebee

items.title: Generative models are often compared using held-out examples, but unlike classification, there is no...
items.content:
Generative models are often compared using held-out examples, but unlike classification, there is no single agreed measure of their overall quality. A score can also be misleading even when the metric is clearly defined: rare examples may strongly affect a metric while being absent from any practical test sample. The article asks which measures of model performance can be compared reliably using a finite set of independent examples from the real-world data distribution.

The article develops a mathematical framework for this question and analyzes whether an evaluator can reliably rank two candidate models. It studies metrics based on tests of model outputs, measures of distributional difference, and perplexity, a common likelihood-based score. The results are theoretical: they apply under the framework’s assumptions about the data and candidate models, rather than arising from experiments on deployed systems.

items.title: Deploying multimodal AI systems, which process both text and visual inputs, across cloud and mobile ...
items.content:
Deploying multimodal AI systems, which process both text and visual inputs, across cloud and mobile environments creates severe network bandwidth and storage pressures. Standard image compression algorithms are built primarily for human eyes, while specialized machine-oriented methods focus on narrow tasks like detecting specific objects. Consequently, existing compression approaches degrade the performance of versatile multimodal models across broad real-world tasks, creating an operational bottleneck between transmission efficiency and model accuracy.

The article systematically analyzes how compression artifacts impair visual processing in multimodal models and demonstrates a specialized compression system called CoTAM to reduce data transmission costs without sacrificing reasoning performance.

items.title: I do think any good benchmark should be customizable by the user to weigh towards what they care abo...
items.content:
I do think any good benchmark should be customizable by the user to weigh towards what they care about the most.

This is typically hard to do for benchmarks measured with deterministic metrics. That's why in ParseBench-2, we treated metric design as a goal-oriented optimization problem! 

1. Let the user specify a severity policy for different scenarios
2. Optimize metrics to fit that objective. 

More details in the paper: https://t.co/syVMKqGMBP

items.summary: jerryjliu0 argues benchmarks should be customizable to user priorities, explaining that ParseBench-2 treats metric design as goal-oriented optimization: users specify a severity policy over scenarios and metrics are optimized to fit that objective.
items.reasoning: Original methodological insight on evaluation design from a recognized practitioner (LlamaIndex founder), with a linked paper; moderate engagement but real technical depth.

items.title:
"It's happening anyway" --> Can be used to justify about anything. 

“From the xAI team standpoint, ...
items.content:
"It's happening anyway" --> Can be used to justify about anything. 

“From the xAI team standpoint, we have the choice of being a spectator or a participant.” --> False dichotomy. 

"Is this wise" --> Great question (and no, it's very unwise). And what's the point of AI if it doesn't help us make wiser decisions?

Follow-up questions:
- What's the point of technology if it doesn't enable humanity to make meaningful choices? 

- When did technological determinism become a death cult?

items.title: @finnhambly @AbieRohrig Many thanks for the feedback, @finnhambly! We agree that the report over-cla...
items.content: @finnhambly @AbieRohrig Many thanks for the feedback, @finnhambly! We agree that the report over-claims a bit here. The crux framework is meant to capture the most commonly discussed pathway from automating AI R&D to accelerating capabilities. But AI R&D can certainly speed up with humans still in the loop. We note this briefly in Section 2.2: “full automation of AI R&D is not necessary for acceleration. In some standard growth models, a singularity (infinite output in finite time) can occur without full AI R&D automation”. We’ll make this more precise in v2 of the report!

💯

In so many of my purchasing decisions these days I get frustrated that there is nothing that I want and I am getting scalped by crazy high prices for the most ordinary basic stuff

The basic end conclusion then is: I have to rip out the middle men

In case of furniture, the answer is design it myself and go to a carpenter to build it

There's going to be a big revival of artisanal jobs I think

items.title: Current state-of-the-art reasoning models rely on reinforcement learning to solve complex tasks, but...
items.content:
Current state-of-the-art reasoning models rely on reinforcement learning to solve complex tasks, but mainstream reward-maximizing algorithms such as Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) suffer from severe mode collapse. By aggressively optimizing for a single dominant solution path, these methods disregard alternative valid reasoning strategies, leading to repetitive reasoning loops and poor generalization. The article introduces FlowRL, a policy optimization framework that shifts the learning objective from reward maximization to reward distribution matching. The article's main objective is to evaluate whether training a language model to match the full reward distribution via flow balancing improves reasoning diversity and overall problem-solving accuracy compared to standard reward-maximizing reinforcement learning.

FlowRL reformulates reinforcement learning by minimizing the reverse divergence between the policy and a target reward distribution normalized by a learnable partition function. The authors show this approach is gradient-equivalent to the trajectory balance objective in Generative Flow Networks, which jointly optimizes expected reward and policy entropy. To scale this sequence-level concept to complex, long chain-of-thought outputs spanning thousands of tokens, the authors incorporate two critical components: length normalization to prevent gradient explosion across variable sequence lengths, and clipped importance sampling to handle off-policy micro-batch updates. The approach was evaluated on open-source foundation models across two scales (7-billion and 32-billion parameters) using rigorous mathematical benchmarks (including AIME, AMC, MATH-500, and OlympiadBench) and coding suites (LiveCodeBench, CodeForces, and HumanEval+), alongside standard cross-domain evaluations.

items.title: .@devonzuegel just secured approval to build an entire village, "Esmeralda," an hour north of San Fr...
items.content:
.@devonzuegel just secured approval to build an entire village, "Esmeralda," an hour north of San Francisco.

Think of it as a "college campus for families": a walkable village with daily lectures, workshops, classes, and kids' camps.

"I like to talk about in terms of both the hardware and the software. The hardware is the physical design. We're building this walkable community.

"Picture the villages that are just on train lines off of cities like Tokyo or Paris or London. They're compact, and so you can walk everywhere."

"On the software side, that’s the part that makes what we're doing more unique.

"It's inspired by a place called Chautauqua, a small town in Western New York that I grew up going to. Think of it almost like a college campus for families, where every day they have lectures, workshops, kids camps, classes."

"You go to college, and you make a lot of your friends through the classes you're taking cause you have this shared interest or shared trials and tribulations of a hard exam."

"I know people in Chautauqua better than I know in my hometown, even though I would only spend summers there. We're basically building a Chautauqua of the West in California."
@esmeralda_inst

items.title: .@devonzuegel explains why Americans pay a fortune to live in walkable villages, yet the US barely b...
items.content:
.@devonzuegel explains why Americans pay a fortune to live in walkable villages, yet the US barely builds them anymore:

"Just getting the permission to build anything, not even anything innovative, but just anything, is really hard, especially in California."

"Because it's so hard to build anything at all, people are then very conservative when they can build. They're like, 'I just wanna build something that I know is gonna sell.' It really ends up dampening down innovation."

"Is it really innovation? This is how people used to live for thousands of years. It's only in the last 75 years since the advent of the car that we've stopped building in this compact, walkable way."

"We treat those small villages and towns that are very walkable like it's a scarce resource that we can't build more of. And as a result, the housing prices in those towns are just insane."

"When you get to the finish line, you’re like, 'Just put anything up. We're not gonna try to build something special here.'"
@esmeralda_inst

#BigData #Analytics #AI #MachineLearning...
items.content:
Buying Tokens vs Building an AI Factory!  @samcharrington 

#BigData #Analytics #AI #MachineLearning #DataScience #AI #IoT #IIoT #Python #RStats #TensorFlow #JavaScript #ReactJS #CloudComputing #Serverless #DataScientist #Linux #Programming #Coding #100DaysofCode 

An AI agent can make many model calls to finish a single job. Some need frontier reasoning. Others can run on an open-weight model, and some involve data that has to stay in-house. How do you decide which inference to buy and which to run yourself?

Sadeepa Wijesekara, who leads engineering for HPE Private Cloud AI, joins Sam Charrington to discuss how enterprises make those decisions. They get into what it takes to see the cost of individual calls, how teams route work between hosted and local models, and when running your own GPUs makes economic sense. Sadeepa shares how HPE routes coding requests through a single internal endpoint that can send work to a frontier provider or serve it locally.

items.title: A free online book: Error-Correction Coding and Decoding by Martin Tomlinson, Cen Jung Tjhai, Marcel...
items.content:
A free online book: Error-Correction Coding and Decoding by Martin Tomlinson, Cen Jung Tjhai, Marcel A. Ambroze, Mohammed Ahmed, and Mubarak Jibril.

Error-correction coding and decoding are fundamental to computer science because they enable reliable data transmission, storage, and computation across inherently noisy physical hardware.

By adding structured mathematical redundancy to binary data, error-correcting codes (ECC) allow systems to detect and repair corrupted bits without needing to retransmit the original message.

This book presents error-correcting codes as both mathematical objects whose performance can be measured and engineered systems whose value depends on their decoding methods and applications.

It connects theoretical limits, code design, decoder behavior, and real communication tasks, with particular attention to binary codes and to how code structure influences achievable performance.

Read the book online on @ChapterPal: https://t.co/phxxQBKa77

items.content:
A free online book: Bash Guide for Beginners by Machtelt Garrels.

Bash (short for Bourne-Again SHell) is a command-line shell and scripting language used to interact directly with an operating system through text commands. Created in 1989 by Brian Fox for the GNU Project, it is the default shell on most Linux distributions and is widely available on macOS and Windows.

Bash Guide for Beginners is a practical introduction to shell scripting for people who already use a UNIX or UNIX-like command line and want to automate recurring work. It is especially relevant to power users and system administrators, whose routine tasks often benefit from scripts.

The book assumes basic shell familiarity and teaches Bash through realistic examples and exercises intended to build confidence in writing and improving scripts.

Read the book online on @ChapterPal : https://t.co/7uTUn2QBXx

items.content:
Buying Telecom Intelligence on Websites vs Building Your Own AI Factory!

Searching websites and querying third-party APIs will only take you so far. They provide fragmented snapshots of telephone numbers, carrier switching, number porting, SIM swaps, geolocation signals, and fraud indicators not a continuously learning intelligence system.

Why keep buying isolated intelligence when you can build the factory that produces it? That’s how you can trace the origins of text messages and missed calls! 

An enterprise-grade Telecom AI Factory integrates authorized carrier-network data, event streaming, graph databases, GPU-accelerated computing, machine learning, and agentic AI to analyze millions of telephone numbers, correlate carrier changes, identify coordinated fraud networks, and detect emerging threats at scale.

Websites deliver information. APIs deliver signals. AI factories transform data into continuously evolving intelligence.

Building your own factory doesn't eliminate the need for licensed telecom data, lawful location access, or public carrier integrations. Infrastructure alone cannot invent information it cannot access.

The competitive advantage isn't merely owning GPUs or buying tokens it's owning the intelligence architecture, data pipelines, proprietary models, and decision-making capabilities!

Exactly, you won't, again that doesn't mean it won't happen just because you don't like it happening?

items.title: A free open online textbook: Structural Design Essentials by by Roel Schipper, Sander Pasterkamp, At...
items.content:
A free open online textbook: Structural Design Essentials by by Roel Schipper, Sander Pasterkamp, Ate Snijder, Marco Schuurman, and Geert Ravenshorst (2024).

Structural Design Essentials is a practical textbook for students and beginning structural designers, connecting structural mechanics and mathematics with the broader work of designing buildings and other structures.

It presents design as an iterative process shaped by project goals, constraints, structural concepts, materials, construction, and verification.

Readers learn to move from defining a project and comparing structural concepts to estimating dimensions, checking performance, and validating a preliminary design against applicable codes.

The book of 148 pages has more than 500 illustrations.
